speaker: Doctor
text: Please tell me, how long have you been experiencing the increasing pain and swelling in your right knee?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the detailed history. The combination of asymmetric oligoarthritis (right knee, resolved left ankle), urethritis (pain with urination), and high-risk sexual behavior strongly suggests an infectious etiology. REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis, Urine Culture, and Blood work including ESR, CRP, and HLA-B27. Do you have any history of psoriasis, eye inflammation, or bowel issues?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis: Protein Negative, Blood Negative, WBC 12–16/hpf, RBC 1–2/hpf; Erythrocyte_Sedimentation_Rate (ESR): 38 mm/h; CRP: Not provided; HLA-B27: Not provided.

speaker: Doctor
text: The urinalysis confirms a significant white blood cell count indicating inflammation or infection, though the HLA-B27 and CRP results are pending. Given your history of a self-resolving ankle joint, do you notice any stiffness in your joints in the morning, or have you experienced eye redness or pain?
